description: Hard - Advanced Concepts of SSL and Domains

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which of the following correctly describe the role of nginx in a typical DigitalOcean + Docker + nginx production deployment?
options: nginx listens on port 443 and presents the SSL certificate to browsers
nginx handles TLS termination and proxies decrypted traffic to the backend
nginx directly handles all database queries to reduce backend load
nginx allows the Spring Boot backend to operate without handling TLS directly
nginx obtains and renews Let's Encrypt certificates via Certbot
nginx serves as the entry point where encrypted traffic becomes unencrypted

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which of the following statements about Let's Encrypt certificates are correct?
options: They are free and issued automatically
They are valid for 90 days and should be renewed automatically
They provide the same padlock indicator to users as paid EV certificates
They require a paid subscription after the first issuance
They can issue wildcard certificates but require DNS challenge validation
The short 90-day validity period limits damage from a compromised certificate

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: A developer receives the NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID error on their production site. Which of the following are likely causes or correct responses?
options: The Let's Encrypt certificate has expired
Certbot's automatic renewal cron job has failed or is not running
The developer should manually run Certbot to renew the certificate
The error means the server's domain name does not match the certificate
The developer should check Certbot logs to diagnose the renewal failure
The error indicates a self-signed certificate is being used in production

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which of the following correctly describe the TLS handshake process?
options: The browser sends the encryption methods it supports to the server
The server presents its SSL certificate during the handshake
The browser verifies the certificate's domain, expiry, and CA trust
The handshake transfers user data before the encrypted channel is established
Browser and server exchange encryption keys to establish the secure channel
The handshake typically adds around 50-100 milliseconds to the first connection

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which of the following are valid uses of self-signed certificates?
options: Local development environments where traffic never leaves your machine
Internal tools accessed only within a trusted private network
Production sites serving real users requiring browser trust
Testing TLS configuration before obtaining a CA-signed certificate
Public-facing APIs that third-party clients will connect to
Staging environments accessible only to the development team internally

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which statements correctly describe wildcard certificates?
options: A wildcard certificate for *.myapp.com covers api.myapp.com and staging.myapp.com
A wildcard certificate covers the root domain myapp.com itself
Wildcard certificates from Let's Encrypt require DNS challenge validation
A single wildcard certificate can replace multiple individual subdomain certificates
Wildcard certificates are only available from paid Certificate Authorities
A wildcard certificate for *.myapp.com would also cover sub.api.myapp.com

questions.question: SELECT ALL THAT APPLY: Which of the following correctly describe why HTTPS is mandatory for production applications?
options: Without HTTPS, passwords and sensitive data travel as readable plain text
Modern browsers display 'Not Secure' warnings for HTTP sites
Some browsers block form submissions over HTTP entirely
HTTPS is only required for e-commerce sites handling payment data
HTTPS prevents man-in-the-middle attacks where traffic could be intercepted
HTTP sites are blocked by all major browsers regardless of content type
